newsitem.title: USA: US Commerce official sees Q2 growth of about 3 pct.
newsitem.headline: US Commerce official sees Q2 growth of about 3 pct.

text.p: The economy has momentum after its strong performance in first three months of 1997 and looks set to grow somewhere around three percent in the second quarter, a senior Commerce Department official said Wednesday.
"The economy now has a lot of momentum," Commerce Undersecretary Everett Ehrlich told Reuters Financial Television in an interview.
But he played down concerns that the strong economic growth could fuel inflation.
The Commerce Department reported earlier that the economy grew by 5.6 percent in the first quarter, fueled by a surge in domestic demand.

Ehrlich was upbeat about the outlook. Consumers remain confident. Inventories are still lagging sales despite their recent rise. And net exports, which were a big drag on growth in the first quarter, are likely to be flat in the second.
"(Growth) well could be at three (percent) or in the environs thereof (in the second quarter)," Ehrlich said.
Ehrlich said that corporate profits look to have been good in the first quarter, growing at an annualized pace of around 15 percent.
The Commerce official acknowledged that inflation had to be a source of concern but said he saw no signs that it was about to surge.

"Inflation has to be a concern when we are this far in the business cycle," Ehrlich said. "At the same time we have to look for real evidence of surges in inflation and I don't think we see real evidence of an imminent danger."
